text.text: crumb: how does a running state-mode session autosave storage state to the vault?
New engineers · Timer-driven saves in supervise(): snapshot cookies, localStorage and IndexedDB, merge with the vault entry, rewrite it.
Local host; all three as one OS user

Owned child, temp
profile; close skips
save

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient, response included;
dashed (async) = event/stream; solid (sync) = awaited request/reply; dotted (local) = file/IPC.

Default 30s; --autosave 0 = no timer. Ticks
join an in-flight save; unchanged snapshot
skips. Errors only go to run/<id>.log; before
advances on success, so next tick retries.

Step 4: cookies and localStorage merge per
key (before→after diff) onto the fresh read;
IndexedDB is copied whole per snapshot
origin. No lock: writes in the 3→5 window are
lost.

Key cached at startup (CRUMB_KEY or
config.json keyStore); missing key fails
launch. Only entry bodies are AES-256-GCM;
header and run/ handle (lastSavedAt) are
plaintext.

Outside this view: Launch/handshake, signal-driven saves (crumb sync, crumb close); Profile mode (same timer, persistent profile), agent CDP,
login/check.
